text:
Jack Eichel still looks like one of the best two-way centers in hockey: 29 points in 24 games, 13 on the power play, and Vegas winning 56% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) with him on at 5v5. His skating data is elite: 96th percentile in top speed, and his 115 bursts over 20 mph rank at the very top of the league.

The cracks are recent. Jesse Granger of The Athletic noted he has "only 3 points at even strength over the last 12 games. A rare rough patch for him." Our numbers agree something is off: nine points in his last ten against 12.4 expected, and Vegas has gone four games without a win, three of them overtime losses, two of those to Dallas this week.

There is also a luck flag pointing the other way. Vegas has scored 6.3 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, which is padding the season line. Evolving-Hockey had him sixth among all forwards in wins above replacement last season, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking ranked him 98th percentile in setting up shots. The playmaking is real. Watch the even-strength points.
headline: Eichel's rare rough patch
